_note: Single source of truth for every number in the Stage 1 submission. Nulls and empty lists fail the gates, so nothing here survives as a placeholder, and a string in a numeric field fails too. Week 2 fills geometry, operating, performance, efficiency, the candidate and sensitivity tables, power_by_radius, mass_envelope_g and sources. Week 3 fills pitch, pitch_schedule, vector_map and packaging. Week 4 fills structure, mass_budget_g and the remaining results. Hard limits are checked against values RECOMPUTED from geometry and the mass lines, so an optimistic headline number achieves nothing. mass_envelope_g lines are {item, nominal_g, conservative_g, basis, scaling_class} with distinct item names. mass_budget_g lines are {item, mass_g, conservative_g, basis, refines}, where refines names the mass_envelope_g item this line came from, so week 4 continuity is checked per component and not only on the total, and conservative_g is what builds results.mass_g_conservative rather than a growth rate chosen after seeing the target. See D33. Aerodynamic power is bounded below by momentum theory over the declared momentum_area_m2, which may not exceed 2R times span, and the figure of merit that falls out has to be credible for a cyclorotor. thrust_sensitivity freezes in week 2 what raising thrust costs, and week 4 may only choose a row from it. Structural demands are derived: per-blade mass from the blade budget and blade count, rotor shaft torque from shaft power and speed, blade root bending from thrust per blade, lever arm and load factor. Row shapes for the remaining lists, so nothing sits in the schema without one: configuration_candidates {config, rotors, module_mass_g, thrust_N, module_tw, selected}, 3 or more; coefficient_scenarios {name, blade_area_coeff, basis, evidence_class}, 3 or more, where evidence_class is measured, derived or downside and a transferred value is never called measured, and a measured row also declares solidity and chord_to_radius so the gate can test whether it was taken on this design's own shape family; aero_azimuthal_loads {azimuth_deg, normal_force_N}, 24 or more; drive_candidates {name, continuous_power_W, continuous_torque_Nm, mass_g, selected}, 2 or more; linkage_dimensions {link, length_mm}, 4 or more; pitch_schedule {azimuth_deg, pitch_deg}, 24 or more; vector_map {phase_command_deg, vertical_force_N, lateral_force_N}, 3 or more. Every mass_envelope_g line also carries scaling_class, one of geometry, power or fixed, because the drive is not a fixed mass. Week 4 fills structure, mass_budget_g, bom and the remaining results, and it does so from tools/structure.py rather than by hand: run tools/linkage.py --write first when the blade section moves, then tools/structure.py --write. bom lines are {item, category, qty, unit_cost_inr, line_cost_inr, lead_time_weeks, make_or_buy, source, priced_date}, where the price is a distributor list level estimate and not an obtained quotation and they carry no physical unit, so nothing in the narrative coverage gate reads them as forces or masses. The structure block carries both the operating case and a declared overspeed: centrifugal load goes as the square of rotor speed, so blade_attachment_margin_overspeed and blade_combined_margin_overspeed are the margins that actually decide the blade, and the gate recomputes both from overspeed_factor. blade_margin is aerodynamic bending alone and is the smaller of the two spanwise loads on a cyclorotor, which is why blade_combined_margin exists beside it.

coefficient_scenarios.name: K19 optimum rotor, measured on this shape family
coefficient_scenarios.basis: Kellen 2019, Table 2.1 configuration 8, printed p.17: 5.5 in chord, 3 blades, 8.25 in radius, 22 in span, NACA 0020, pitch amplitude 40 degrees. CT/sigma read off the vector path data of Fig 3.25 (1.04424) and Fig 3.28 (1.04428), which agree to 0.003 percent, then converted by coeff = (2/pi)(CT/sigma) out of Kellen's projected area convention A = span times 2R. Measured on Kellen's rotor and not on ours, and that rotor's solidity and chord to radius sit within 1.1 percent of this design's. Chord Reynolds 186,000, inside the 100,000 to 300,000 band that also contains this design's 134,074

coefficient_scenarios.name: S2 quad rotor hover point, corrected against the primary source
coefficient_scenarios.basis: Benedict 2010 printed p.236: at the operating RPM of 1800, each rotor produced around 1.91 N of thrust. Printed p.225 gives the same point as 195 grams at 1800 rpm and 40 degrees pitching amplitude. Four NACA 0010 blades of 33.0 mm chord and 158.8 mm span at 76.2 mm radius, printed p.220 and p.233. Recomputed in this project's blade area convention. This is the transfer the nominal should have rested on, and its chord Reynolds is 31,600 rather than the 35,100 the ledger carried

coefficient_scenarios.name: nominal, held at 0.6055 rather than raised
coefficient_scenarios.basis: the value the rest of the design is built on. Its arithmetic used 1.98 N at 2000 rpm, which is the 809 gram all-up vehicle weight of Benedict's Table 5.1 divided by four, paired with the twin rotor's operating speed. The source states neither as a quad thrust. All three measured or corrected points now sit above 0.6055, so the old error ran in the safe direction and the gap is held as deliberate margin rather than spent. See D36

coefficient_scenarios.name: S2 twin rotor, three blades at the same radius and speed
coefficient_scenarios.basis: 1.47 N per rotor, half of the 300 grams total Benedict 2010 printed p.229 reports at 2000 rpm, on three blades of 25.4 mm chord and 152.4 mm span at 76.2 mm radius, recomputed the same way. The source rounds the same quantity to 1.5 N per rotor on printed p.232. Higher than the quad but at a solidity of 0.159, far outside the measured band, so it is carried as an upside indication and not adopted

coefficient_scenarios.name: blade deflection loss only
coefficient_scenarios.basis: the nominal less a 5 percent thrust loss for blade bending and torsion, sized against the computed section stiffness rather than assumed. This is the low coefficient the conservative case now runs on, because the Kellen measurement retired the other allowance. See D35

coefficient_scenarios.name: deflection loss and configuration transfer, retired
coefficient_scenarios.basis: the nominal less 5 percent for blade flexibility and a further 10 percent for a transfer that changed blade count, airfoil and chord ratio at once with nothing measured to de-risk it. Retired on 31 August 2026 when Kellen came in at 0.6648, measured on this design's own shape family and above the nominal, which is the test D23 set. Kept as the record of what the conservative case used to be

performance.blade_area_coeff: Benedict 2010, quad-cyclocopter rotor at hover. The repository carried 1.98 N per rotor at 2000 rpm, a pair the source never states: printed p.236 gives 1.91 N at 1800 rpm and printed p.225 gives 195 grams at the same speed, and those recompute to 0.7211 in this convention. 0.6055 is held anyway per D36, so nothing downstream moves upward on a correction. Derived, never measured on this configuration
performance.blade_area_coeff_low: The nominal less the 5 percent blade deflection allowance and nothing else. The 10 percent configuration-transfer allowance retired when Kellen 2019 came in at 0.6648, measured on this shape family and above the nominal, which is the test D23 set. Still an engineering downside scenario rather than a published lower bound. See D35
performance.momentum_area_m2: Projected frontal area 2R times span, the standard cyclorotor momentum closure and the cap the gate applies
performance.power_loading_ref_N_per_W: Benedict 2010 twin-cyclorotor at its operating point, printed p.232: at the operating thrust of 1.5 N (per rotor), the power loading of the rotor was 0.062 N/W. The quad reaches 0.076 N/W on printed p.236, so 0.062 is the lower of the two measured routes and it is the one used
performance.blade_deflection_thrust_loss: Bounded from above by the computed blade section, not derived from it: EI 66.8 Nm2 gives 0.086 mm of tip deflection and GJ 9.6 Nm2 gives 0.054 degrees of twist, so the section alone supports well under 1 percent. The 5 percent is carried as a floor over build tolerance, bond line variation and unsteady effects the section does not model
performance.figure_of_merit: Kellen 2019 section 3.3, read off the thesis rather than a summary: the peak figure of merit was found to be 0.6, on a 3-bladed cyclorotor with a 5.5in chord, 22in. span, and 8.25 in radius. Reading CT/sigma off Fig 3.25 and CP/sigma off Fig 3.26 for that rotor and closing FM = CT^1.5/(sqrt(2)*CP) gives 0.595, so the stated value reproduces to 0.8 percent
performance.reynolds: 134,074 at the design point, inside the 100,000 to 300,000 band Kellen measured this shape family across, and Kellen's own optimum rotor sits at 186,000. The 100,000 ceiling D25 rested on comes from Shrestha and Benedict and still bounds the Benedict-derived nominal, but the shape family now carries a measured coefficient bracketing the design point. See D37
performance.motor_derate: 0.80 applied to the T-Motor 180 second Max Power and Peak Current to get a continuous figure. It has no source and the problem statement asks for no endurance, so nothing outside the design sets it. What is bounded instead is the consequence: motor_current_frac_180s is the derate at which the selected motor stops covering the design point
performance.motor_current_frac_180s: design point current over the published 180 second peak. It doubles as the break even derate, because the selection holds exactly while the derate stays above the fraction being drawn. For a demonstration inside 180 seconds it is the headroom on the datasheet number itself
performance.motor_speed_ceiling_rpm: KV times the pack voltage after the resistive drop at the working current, on 6 cells at 3.70 V nominal. motor_speed_rule is the 90 percent of it that week 2 screened belt ratios against, which is the rule that emptied the 100 mm radius row and which lived in prose until now
performance.thrust_floor_stacked_N: design thrust the stacked downside needs to hold thrust to weight 2.5, from the conservative mass and the coefficient haircut. It is what stops the design point being lowered to relieve the drive: no row of thrust_sensitivity below the design point clears it

structure.blade_root_bending_Nm: aerodynamic bending at mid span. The blade is held at both spiders, so a uniformly distributed peak load gives a lever of span over 8, 36.30 mm. The load is thrust per blade times the 4.0 peak to mean factor D16 sets, which is the top of the published 3 to 4 range because that range is simulated. The rerun week 3 model gives 2.501 and is not used here
structure.shaft_torque_Nm: aerodynamic power plus tare, divided by rotor angular speed at 2404.79 rpm. This is the rotor shaft, downstream of the 3.5 to 1 belt reduction. It reproduces the rotor_torque_Nm week 2 published in the sensitivity table
structure.pitch_link_load_N: peak pitch link force from the week 3 four-bar solution, rerun in tools/linkage.py against the week 4 blade. The blade is not chordwise balanced, so this is the unbalanced figure per D43, and the centrifugal pitching moment on the 9.31 percent chord offset is most of it
structure.blade_allowable_Nm: bending capacity of the closed cell section about the chord line, from the integrated NACA 0020 ordinates. The skin governs at 215 MPa of wrinkling stress over the foam, not at the 400 MPa laminate allowable, and the spar would take 63.2 Nm before the skin takes 25.3
structure.blade_attachment_allowable_N: two 693ZZ pitch bearings per blade at a 270 N static rating each, supplier listing. They are the softest element in the path from the blade to the spider arm, softer than the bonded root fitting or the bracket bolts
structure.overspeed_factor: 20 percent over the design rotor speed, covering ESC control overshoot and a gust transient. The problem statement sets no endurance or speed schedule, so this is a declared case rather than a derived one
structure.pitch_bearing_recirculation_ratio: cage swing over ball spacing for the 693ZZ at the 80 degrees of pitch travel the four-bar gives. Cage swing is (1 - d/Dm)/2 of the inner ring angle with a stationary outer ring, d and Dm from catalogue geometry and a 7 ball complement. Below 1.0 each ball stays inside its own arc, so the wear mode is false brinelling and not fatigue. The ratio only reaches 1.0 at 144.6 degrees of travel, which no cyclorotor pitch schedule asks for, so the regime cannot be tuned out and has to be carried
structure.pitch_bearing_static_safety: 693ZZ static rating over the centrifugal pull per bearing at the operating speed, which is where wear accumulates. The overspeed case is strength and it is gated separately on blade_attachment_margin_overspeed. The 2.0 floor is a declared rule for a bearing that does not fully recirculate, in the same class of judgement as overspeed_factor, and Stage 2 closes it with a run to failure rather than with a catalogue number
structure.pitch_bearing_friction_W: 0.5 x mu x P x d summed over six bearings at the mean swing rate, mu taken at 0.0015 for a deep groove ball bearing. It is under a tenth of a percent of rotor shaft power, which is why it sits outside the power budget rather than inside it. The PTFE fabric lined plain bearing that would be immune to the wear mode costs pitch_bearing_plain_alternative_W instead, on a 0.08 liner friction coefficient, and that is the trade Stage 2 makes

efficiency.transmission: Single stage toothed belt at 0.93. Assumed, not measured. Published belt drive efficiency runs 0.95 to 0.98 at these speeds, so this is on the pessimistic side of the range
efficiency.motor: Outrunner at 0.84. Assumed, not measured, and the sensitivity matters: at 0.78 the motor input rises to 552 W and the selected drive is at its rating
efficiency.esc: Brushless controller at 0.95. Assumed, not measured, and the least sensitive link in the chain

drive.continuous_rating: T-Motor publishes Max. Power (180s) and Peak Current (180s), which is a three minute maximum and not an indefinite hover rating. Week 2 derates both by 0.80 for continuous duty. The derate is a judgement, stated rather than hidden, because the problem statement gives no endurance requirement to size it against
drive.belt_ratio: Smallest ratio at which motor torque stays inside the derated continuous torque and motor speed stays under 90 percent of what the 6S pack can turn it at, allowing for the internal resistance drop at the working current

thrust_sensitivity.drive_consequence: MN5006 KV450 at 2.5 to 1 covers it with the most room of any row, 12.65 A of the 20.8 A continuous
MN5006 KV450 at 3.5 to 1, 17.27 A of the 20.8 A continuous
MN5006 KV450 at 3.5 to 1, 20.61 A of the 20.8 A continuous and 8417 of 9435 motor rpm. The design point, and the tightest row that still fits

no shortlist drive fits at this radius. The motor input of 512.6 W is inside the 520 W continuous, but the torque wants a belt ratio the KV450 cannot spin to on 6S, which is why raising thrust stops paying here
